thread.title: Dayton Fire Department introduces free 'File for Life' emergency information program
thread.title_full: Dayton Fire Department introduces free 'File for Life' emergency information program

author: Buckeye Reporter
title: Dayton Fire Department introduces free 'File for Life' emergency information program
text:
The Dayton Fire Department announced on May 27 the launch of File for Life, a free tool designed to help first responders quickly access critical medical information during emergencies.
The File for Life program provides residents with an easy-to-complete form where they can list important details such as medications, medical conditions, allergies, and emergency contacts. Residents are encouraged to fill out the form and place it on their refrigerator so that first responders can locate it easily when responding to calls. The department said this step can save valuable time when seconds matter.
According to the department, File for Life is available at no cost to all Dayton residents. The initiative supports Dayton’s ongoing commitment as an Age-Friendly City and is part of the broader Age-Friendly Dayton Plan aimed at helping residents of all ages live safely, remain active, and thrive in their community.
Residents interested in participating can download the form or call 937-333-5555 or 937-333-4520 for assistance. Additional safety resources are also available through these channels.
Dayton delivers municipal services through departments focused on public safety, public works, recreation, and economic development; it operates under a council-manager government structure with an elected mayor and city commission that appoints a professional city manager, and it promotes community engagement by providing accessible agendas, minutes, boards, commissions, and public meetings—all according to the official website .
